introduction: Today we celebrate the Transfiguration of the Lord. On a high mountain, Jesus' face shines like the sun before Peter, James and John, and the Father says, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him. Daniel sees one like a son of man receiving an everlasting kingdom. Peter writes that he was an eyewitness of Christ's majesty. Let us listen to the beloved Son.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Father has revealed the glory of his beloved Son. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may listen to the beloved Son and reflect his light. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are in darkness: that the morning star may rise in their hearts. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace in the world, especially in places torn by war: that the light of Christ may overcome violence. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are afraid: that Jesus may touch them and say, Rise, and do not be afraid. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may be transformed by spending time in the presence of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, on the holy mountain you revealed the glory of your beloved Son. Help us to listen to him, and transform us by his light. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: His face shone like the sun
reflection.body:
This feast takes us back to the mountain where Jesus revealed his glory to three of his disciples. Matthew tells us that Jesus "was changed before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light." Moses and Elijah, representing the Law and the Prophets, appear and speak with him.

Peter, overwhelmed, wants to stay: "Lord, it is good for us to be here." He offers to make three tents. But while he is still speaking, "a bright cloud overshadowed them," and the Father's voice is heard: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him." The disciples fall to the ground in fear. Then Jesus comes and touches them. When they look up, "they saw no one, except Jesus alone."

Daniel's vision helps us understand who this is. He sees "one like a son of man" who comes to the Ancient of Days and receives "Dominion... with glory and a kingdom." "His dominion is an everlasting dominion." The glory the disciples saw was the glory of the Son of Man, whom all nations will serve.

Peter never forgot this day. Years later he wrote: "we didn't follow cunningly devised fables... but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty." He tells us to hold on to the word of God "as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star arises in your hearts."

The Transfiguration is a promise. The glory that shone in Jesus is meant to transform us too. This happens slowly, as we spend time in his presence, in prayer and the sacraments.

Today, spend a few quiet minutes with Jesus, perhaps before the Blessed Sacrament. Listen to him. And let his light reach whatever is dark in your life.
